我 听懂 老师 说 的 话 了
我 可以 听 老师 说 的 话
我 听见 老师 但 不懂
exercises.answer: 我 听懂 老师 说 的 话 了
exercises.explanation: 听 = listen. 听懂 = listen + understand. Without 懂, you've only listened — you might not have followed the meaning.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the result: "我 看 了 那 本 书, 但 没 看 ___ 完" (I read that book but didn't finish)
exercises.explanation: 完 = finished. 看完 = read to completion. 没 看完 = didn't finish reading.

exercises.prompt: Pick the contrast: "我 听 了 这 首 歌" vs "我 听懂 了 这 首 歌"
options: First = listened; second = listened AND understood
First is past, second is future
exercises.answer: First = listened; second = listened AND understood
exercises.explanation: 听 alone is just the action. 听懂 adds the result of comprehension.

exercises.prompt: Build "I didn't see her" (i.e. I looked but didn't manage to see her)
exercises.answer: 我 没 看见 她
exercises.explanation: Negate the WHOLE resultative compound with 没: 没 看见, not 看 没 见.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct way to say "I can't understand him" (in the comprehension sense)?
options: 我 不 听 他
我 不 可以 听懂 他
我 听 不 懂 他
我 没 听 他
exercises.answer: 我 听 不 懂 他
exercises.explanation: Potential complement: 不 sits INSIDE between verb and result. 听不懂 = unable to understand by listening.

exercises.source: 我 看见 你 了
exercises.explanation: 看见 = the result was achieved — you were actually perceived. 了 marks the change of state.

exercises.prompt: "老师 说 得 太 快, 我 ___" — fill in "I didn't catch it"
exercises.explanation: 没 听懂 = listened but didn't manage to understand. Classic complaint about fast speakers.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.spokenText: 你 看见 我 的 钥匙 了 吗
options: 你 看见 我 的 钥匙 了 吗
你 看 我 的 钥匙 了 吗
你 听见 我 的 钥匙 了 吗
你 找 我 的 钥匙 了 吗
exercises.answer: 你 看见 我 的 钥匙 了 吗
exercises.explanation: 看见 (kàn jiàn) — "see" with the result baked in. The right way to ask "did you see my keys?"

exercises.prompt: Build "I heard the bell" (i.e. perceived the sound)
exercises.answer: 我 听见 铃声 了
exercises.explanation: 听见 = listen + perceive. Use this — not just 听 — when reporting that a sound reached you.

exercises.prompt: Translate 我 听 不 懂 to natural English
exercises.explanation: Potential complement 听不懂 → "can't understand (by listening)". English uses the modal "can't" + bare verb — no "am", no double negative.

exercises.prompt: Which means "see (perceive)"?
Build "Did you hear me?"
exercises.answer: 你 听见 我 了 吗

exercises.prompt: Fill the result: "我 听 ___ 了 你 的 话" (heard/understood)
What does "我 听不懂" mean?
Tap what you hear
Build "I saw your message"
exercises.answer: 我 看见 你 的 信息 了

exercises.prompt: Why use 看见 not just 看?
options: 看见 includes the result of seeing; 看 is just the action of looking
看见 is past; 看 is future
exercises.answer: 看见 includes the result of seeing; 看 is just the action of looking

exercises.source: I didn't hear what he said
exercises.answer: 我 没 听见 他 说 什么

exercises.prompt: Fill: "老师 的 字 太 小, 我 看 ___ 见" (negative result)

lessons.title: 学会 / 学完 / 学好
lessons.description: Same verb 学, three different results

exercises.prompt: "我 学会 了 开车" means:
options: I learned to drive (and can do it now)
I want to learn to drive
exercises.answer: I learned to drive (and can do it now)
exercises.explanation: 学会 = study + can. The result is acquired SKILL. You can now do the thing.

exercises.prompt: "我 学完 了 这 本 书" means:
options: I finished studying this book (got to the end)
exercises.answer: I finished studying this book (got to the end)
exercises.explanation: 学完 = study + finish. Completion of the material, not necessarily mastery.

exercises.prompt: Contrast: "我 学完 了 中文" vs "我 学会 了 中文"
options: First: I finished my Chinese course. Second: I actually know Chinese.
First: I know Chinese. Second: I started Chinese.
exercises.answer: First: I finished my Chinese course. Second: I actually know Chinese.
exercises.explanation: 完 = endpoint reached. 会 = ability acquired. You can finish a textbook without mastering the language.

exercises.prompt: "我 要 把 这 个 问题 学好" means:
options: I want to finish this topic
I want to study this topic well (thoroughly)
I want to like this topic
I want to skip this topic
exercises.answer: I want to study this topic well (thoroughly)
exercises.explanation: 学好 = study + well. 好 as a complement signals doing the action thoroughly / to a good standard.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "作业 我 还 没 做 ___" (I haven't finished the homework)
exercises.explanation: 做完 = do + finish. Pair 没 with 完 to say the task isn't yet complete.

exercises.prompt: Build "He hasn't learned how to swim yet" (still doesn't have the skill)
exercises.answer: 他 还 没 学会 游泳
exercises.explanation: Negate 学会 with 没. 还 没 学会 = hasn't yet acquired the skill.

exercises.prompt: Which complement fits "finished cooking"?
options: Either 做完 or 做好
exercises.answer: Either 做完 or 做好
exercises.explanation: 做完 = reached the end. 做好 = done well / ready to serve. Both are common; speakers pick based on emphasis.

exercises.source: 我 学会 弹 钢琴 了
acceptableAnswers: I have learned to play piano
I learned how to play the piano
exercises.explanation: 学会 + verb-object = acquired the skill of doing X. 了 confirms the state change.

exercises.prompt: Your teacher says "请 把 作业 做好". She wants you to:
options: Finish the homework as fast as possible
exercises.explanation: 做好 emphasizes quality / readiness, not just completion.

exercises.prompt: Which pair contrasts results correctly?
options: 学完 = finished; 学会 = mastered the skill
学完 = liked it; 学会 = read it
学完 = started; 学会 = stopped
exercises.answer: 学完 = finished; 学会 = mastered the skill
exercises.explanation: 完 marks endpoint. 会 marks acquired ability. They answer different questions about the same verb.

exercises.prompt: Which complement marks completion?
Build "I haven't finished reading this book"
exercises.answer: 我 还 没 看 完 这 本 书

exercises.prompt: Fill: "妈妈 还 没 ___ 完 饭" (做 — cook)
What does "学会" (xué huì) mean?
Tap what you hear
Build "Have you finished your homework?"
exercises.answer: 你 作业 做 完 了 吗

exercises.prompt: Pick the right complement: "He cooked the food well"
options: 他 把 饭 做 好 了
他 把 饭 做 见 了
他 把 饭 做 会 了
他 把 饭 做 出 了
exercises.answer: 他 把 饭 做 好 了

exercises.source: I finally learned how to drive
exercises.answer: 我 终于 学会 了 开 车

exercises.prompt: Fill: "我 还 没 ___ 完 这 个 项目" (做 — finish doing)
Pick the difference: 做 完 vs 做 好
options: 做 完 = finished (done with); 做 好 = done well / properly
完 is future, 好 is past
exercises.answer: 做 完 = finished (done with); 做 好 = done well / properly

lessons.title: Directional: 上 / 下 / 进 / 出
lessons.description: Verb + direction — walk up onto, take down, run out of

exercises.prompt: Build "He walked up onto the stage"
exercises.answer: 他 走 上 舞台
exercises.explanation: 走上 = walk + onto / up. The direction follows the verb directly.

exercises.prompt: "她 跑 出 教室" means:
options: She runs out of the classroom
She walks out of the classroom
exercises.answer: She runs out of the classroom
exercises.explanation: 跑 = run; 出 = out. Verb + direction = motion + path.

exercises.prompt: Build "Please take the book down (off the shelf)"
exercises.answer: 请 把 书 拿 下 来
exercises.explanation: 拿下来 = take + down + toward speaker. Classic 把-construction with directional.

exercises.prompt: Which means "He walks into the room"?
options: 他 走 上 房间
他 走 进 房间
他 走 出 房间
他 走 下 房间
exercises.answer: 他 走 进 房间
exercises.explanation: 进 = into / enter. Pair it with motion verbs (走, 跑, 跳) for entering.

exercises.prompt: Build "The cat jumped down from the table"
exercises.answer: 猫 从 桌子 上 跳 下 来
exercises.explanation: 跳下来 = jump + down + toward speaker. 从…上 frames the starting point.

exercises.prompt: "他 拿 上 一 杯 茶" means:
options: He takes a cup of tea up / picks up a cup of tea
He drinks a cup of tea
He takes a cup of tea down
He breaks a cup of tea
exercises.answer: He takes a cup of tea up / picks up a cup of tea
exercises.explanation: 拿上 = take + up. Picture lifting it from a surface.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "他 跑 ___ 房间 找 钥匙" (He ran INTO the room to look for keys)
exercises.explanation: 进 = into. 跑进 = run into a space.

exercises.prompt: Which direction fits "take down (from up high)"?
exercises.explanation: 下 = down / off. 拿下 = take down.

exercises.prompt: Build "She ran out of the supermarket"
exercises.answer: 她 跑 出 超市
exercises.explanation: 跑出 = run out (of). The location comes right after.

exercises.prompt: Which is grammatical for "He climbed up the mountain"?
options: 他 上 爬 山
他 爬 上 山
他 山 爬 上
他 上 山 爬
exercises.answer: 他 爬 上 山
exercises.explanation: Verb first, direction second, object last: 爬 (climb) + 上 (up) + 山 (mountain).

exercises.prompt: Which directional means "into"?
Build "He walked into the office"
exercises.answer: 他 走 进 办公室

exercises.prompt: Fill the directional: "她 跑 ___ 房间 了" (out)
What does "拿 出来" (ná chū lái) mean?
Tap what you hear
Build "Take the box down"
exercises.answer: 把 箱子 拿 下 来

exercises.prompt: Pick the right directional: "He climbed up the mountain"
options: 他 爬 上 山
他 爬 下 山
他 爬 进 山
他 爬 出 山
exercises.answer: 他 爬 上 山

exercises.source: She ran out of the room
exercises.answer: 她 跑 出 房间

exercises.prompt: Fill: "小猫 跳 ___ 桌子" (up onto)
What does "飞 上 天" (fēi shàng tiān) mean?

lessons.title: Compound directionals: 上来 / 下去 / 进来 / 出去
lessons.description: Add 来 (toward speaker) or 去 (away from speaker)

exercises.prompt: You're upstairs. Your friend is downstairs. You shout "快 上来!" — what are you telling them?
exercises.explanation: 上来 = up + toward speaker. You're up; they're below; you want them to ascend to YOU.

exercises.prompt: You're upstairs and your friend wants to come up. They look up and say "我 上 ___ 了". Pick the right complement.
exercises.explanation: Speaker is moving TOWARD you (the listener, who is up). From their perspective, you are the destination — 来 (come). 上来 = coming up.

exercises.prompt: Contrast: "她 跑 出 去 了" vs "她 跑 出 来 了"
options: First: ran out (away from speaker). Second: ran out (toward speaker).
First: ran in. Second: ran out.
exercises.answer: First: ran out (away from speaker). Second: ran out (toward speaker).
exercises.explanation: 去 = away from speaker. 来 = toward speaker. The direction relative to YOU is the key insight English doesn't bake into motion verbs.

exercises.prompt: You're inside. Tell someone outside "Come in!"
exercises.explanation: 进来 = enter + toward speaker. Standard invitation to come inside.

exercises.prompt: You're inside. You tell a noisy person "出去!". What did you say?
exercises.explanation: 出去 = out + away from speaker. Sharp dismissal.

exercises.prompt: Build "He walked down (away from me)"
exercises.answer: 他 走 下 去 了
exercises.explanation: 下去 = down + away from speaker. 了 marks the completed motion.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.spokenText: 你 快 上 来 吧
options: 你 快 上 来 吧
你 快 下 去 吧
你 快 进 来 吧
你 快 出 去 吧
exercises.answer: 你 快 上 来 吧
exercises.explanation: 上来 (shàng lái) — come up. Common invitation when speaker is above the listener.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.explanation: 出去 (chū qù) — please go out / leave. Contrast with 进来 (come in).

exercises.prompt: You're at the bottom of the stairs. You call to a friend at the top: "快 ___!" (Come down quickly!)
exercises.explanation: Speaker is below. Friend should DESCEND TOWARD speaker → 下来.

exercises.prompt: Your friend (inside) calls you (outside): "快 进 来 吧!" — what are they saying?
exercises.explanation: 进来 = enter + toward speaker. They're inside; you should enter TOWARD them.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right "come down to me":
Build "I'll come up (to you)" (you're up there)
Fill: "快 ___ 来 吃饭" (downstairs, kids upstairs)
You're outside. Tell your friend (inside) "I'll come in":
Tap what you hear
Build "He walked out" (away from us)
exercises.answer: 他 走 出 去 了

exercises.prompt: Why does direction matter with 来/去?
options: 来 = toward speaker; 去 = away from speaker
exercises.answer: 来 = toward speaker; 去 = away from speaker

exercises.prompt: Fill: "她 跑 出 ___ 了" (toward us)
Pick the right phrase: "He brought it up here" (you're upstairs)
options: 他 拿 上 来 了
他 拿 上 去 了
他 拿 下 来 了
他 拿 进 来 了
exercises.answer: 他 拿 上 来 了

lessons.title: Potential: 看得见 vs 看不见
lessons.description: 得 / 不 inserted INSIDE the complement — not the same as 可以

exercises.prompt: "我 看得见 那 个 招牌" means:
options: I'm not allowed to see the sign
I can see the sign (it's visible to me)
I want to see the sign
I have to see the sign
exercises.answer: I can see the sign (it's visible to me)
exercises.explanation: 看得见 = see-able. 得 sits between 看 and 见 to say the result IS achievable.

exercises.prompt: "我 听不懂 他 说 的 话" means:
options: I refuse to listen to him
I'm not allowed to listen to him
I can't understand what he says (it's not comprehensible to me)
I don't want to listen to him
exercises.answer: I can't understand what he says (it's not comprehensible to me)
exercises.explanation: 听不懂 = un-understandable-by-listening. 不 inserted between 听 and 懂. The result isn't achievable.

exercises.prompt: English-L1 trap: which is WRONG for "I can see"?
options: Both 'B' and 'C' — use potential complement 看得见 for visibility
exercises.answer: Both 'B' and 'C' — use potential complement 看得见 for visibility
exercises.explanation: 可以 / 能 ask about PERMISSION or general capability. 看得见 specifically says "the sight reaches me / is visible." Native speakers say 看得见, not 可以 看见.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "老师 的 字 太 小, 我 看 ___ 见" (I can't see — the writing is too small)
exercises.explanation: Negative potential: 看不见 = can't see. 不 goes between verb and complement.

exercises.prompt: Build "I can understand what you say"
exercises.answer: 我 听得懂 你 说 的 话
exercises.explanation: 听得懂 — single chunk: verb + 得 + result. Don't break it into 可以 + 听懂.

exercises.prompt: "这 道 题 我 做 不 出 来" means:
options: I refuse to do this problem
I haven't done this problem yet
I can't figure out this problem (can't produce a solution)
exercises.answer: I can't figure out this problem (can't produce a solution)
exercises.explanation: 做不出来 = unable to produce / work out. 不 sits inside the verb-complement compound.

exercises.source: 我 看不见 黑板
acceptableAnswers: The blackboard isn't visible to me
exercises.explanation: 看不见 — classic complaint from the back of the classroom.

exercises.prompt: Pick the natural Mandarin for "I can hear it" (the sound reaches me):
exercises.explanation: 听得见 = hear-able. Use for perception capability, not permission.

exercises.prompt: Form the question "Can you understand?" (comprehension):
options: 你 能 听 吗?
你 可以 听 吗?
你 想 听 吗?
exercises.explanation: 听得懂 吗 — standard "do you follow?" Distinct from asking permission.

exercises.prompt: Build "I can't finish this book" (don't have the ability to finish it)
exercises.answer: 我 看 不 完 这 本 书
exercises.explanation: 看不完 = can't finish reading. Different from 没 看完 (haven't finished). 不 = capability; 没 = past fact.

exercises.prompt: What's the difference between 看见 and 看得见?
options: 看见 = past fact 'saw'; 看得见 = current capability 'can see'
exercises.answer: 看见 = past fact 'saw'; 看得见 = current capability 'can see'

exercises.prompt: Build "I can hear it clearly"
exercises.answer: 我 听得 很 清楚

exercises.prompt: Fill: "这 个 字 我 看 ___ 见" (potential: cannot see)
What's the potential form of 听懂?
Tap what you hear
Build "Can you finish reading this book?"
exercises.answer: 你 看得 完 这 本 书 吗

exercises.prompt: Pick the natural negation: "I can't reach the top shelf"
options: 我 够 不 到 顶 上 的 架子
我 没 够 顶 上 的 架子
我 不 够 到 顶 上 的 架子
顶 上 我 够 不 到 的 架子
exercises.answer: 我 够 不 到 顶 上 的 架子

exercises.source: I can understand a little Chinese
exercises.answer: 我 听得 懂 一些 中文

exercises.prompt: Fill: "这 道 题 我 做 ___ 出 来" (can't, potential)
What does "想得起来" mean?

lessons.title: Mixed practice
lessons.description: Resultative + directional + potential — pick the right form

exercises.prompt: Translate: "He climbed up the mountain (and made it to the top)"
options: 他 爬 上 山 了
他 想 爬 山
他 不 爬 山
exercises.answer: 他 爬 上 山 了
exercises.explanation: 爬上 = climb + up (result reached). 了 confirms completion.

exercises.prompt: English-L1 trap: which is WRONG for "I can't understand the news"?
options: 我 听 不 懂 新闻
我 可以 不 听懂 新闻
听 不 懂 新闻
exercises.answer: 我 可以 不 听懂 新闻
exercises.explanation: 可以 不 听懂 is unnatural. Use the potential complement 听不懂 — don't try to bolt 可以 onto a resultative.

exercises.prompt: Build "Please come in" (you're inside; addressee is outside)
exercises.explanation: 进来 = enter + toward speaker. Don't use 进去 here — that pushes them away from you.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural way to say "I learned how to cook"?
options: 我 学 做 菜
我 学会 做 菜 了
我 可以 做 菜
我 想 学 做 菜
exercises.answer: 我 学会 做 菜 了
exercises.explanation: 学会 = study + acquired skill. The result (capability) is the point.

exercises.prompt: Trap: "我 没 看见 你" vs "我 看 不 见 你" — pick the contrast.
options: First: didn't see you (past fact). Second: can't see you (capability now).
exercises.answer: First: didn't see you (past fact). Second: can't see you (capability now).
exercises.explanation: 没 looks back at what happened. 不 inside the complement asks about current capability.

exercises.prompt: Build "She ran out of the house (toward us)"
exercises.answer: 她 跑 出 来 了
exercises.explanation: 跑出来 = run + out + toward speaker. 了 marks completion.

exercises.prompt: "作业 我 还 没 做完, 但 已 经 做 ___ 一半" — fill in (already done half)
exercises.explanation: 已 经 做 了 一半 — neutral past with aspect 了. Don't add 完 if you haven't finished.

exercises.prompt: English-L1 trap: pick the WRONG translation of "I can hear the music"
options: 我 听得见 音乐
我 能 听到 音乐
我 可以 听 音乐
Native uses 听得见 / 听到 — 可以 听 means 'allowed to listen', a different idea
exercises.answer: 我 可以 听 音乐
exercises.explanation: 可以 listen = have permission. Use a potential complement (听得见) or 听到 for actual perception.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
exercises.spokenText: 我 看 不 见 你
options: 我 看 不 见 你
我 没 看见 你
我 可以 看见 你
我 看见 你 了
exercises.answer: 我 看 不 见 你
exercises.explanation: 看不见 (kàn bu jiàn) — "can't see you (right now)." Distinct from 没 看见 (didn't see you).

exercises.prompt: Build "Take the suitcase down (off the rack, toward me)"
exercises.answer: 请 把 行李箱 拿 下 来
exercises.explanation: 拿下来 = take + down + toward speaker. Combines 把-construction with directional complement — peak B1.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right form for "already half-done":
options: 已经 做 了 一半
做 了 一半 已经
已经 一半 做 了
一半 已经 做 了
exercises.answer: 已经 做 了 一半

exercises.prompt: Build "I finally figured it out"
exercises.answer: 我 终于 想 出来 了

exercises.prompt: Fill: "老师 的 话 我 听 ___ 懂 了" (potential: can)
Pick the right complement: "I successfully fixed the computer"
options: 我 把 电脑 修 好 了
我 把 电脑 修 完 了
我 把 电脑 修 见 了
我 把 电脑 修 上 了
exercises.answer: 我 把 电脑 修 好 了

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
Build "He couldn't think of her name"
exercises.answer: 他 想 不 起 她 的 名字

exercises.prompt: Trap: which is WRONG?
options: 我 听得见 音乐
我 看不见 黑板
我 听 不 见 一 下
我 看得见 招牌
exercises.answer: 我 听 不 见 一 下
我 终于 听 懂 了

exercises.prompt: Fill: "我 走 ___ 来" (into, toward us)
Pick the natural sentence: "Please bring up the suitcase"
options: 请 把 行李箱 拿 上 来
请 把 行李箱 拿 上 去
请 把 行李箱 拿 下 来
请 把 行李箱 拿 出 来
exercises.answer: 请 把 行李箱 拿 上 来

topics.title: Measure word deep dive
topics.description: Beyond 个 — picking the right classifier for the noun: 条, 张, 只, 件, 把, 颗, 杯, 瓶 …

guide.intro: In A1 you learned 个 (the universal MW) and 本 (for books). Mandarin actually has hundreds of measure words — but you only need about a dozen to sound natural. The rule of thumb: shape and category of the noun pick the MW.

sections.text: Shape-based MWs

rows: fish, snakes, roads, pants, dogs (slim ones)

sections.text: Category MWs

rows: most animals; one of a pair

sections.text: Native speakers will understand if you say 一 个 鱼 instead of 一 条 鱼 — but you'll sound like a beginner. Picking the right MW is exactly what makes B1 sound like B1.
The 个 trap
English speakers over-use 个 because it's the safest fallback. Push yourself: when you see a long thin thing, reach for 条; flat → 张; clothing → 件; small round → 颗. Build the reflex.

lessons.title: 条 vs 张 — long vs flat
lessons.description: Shape decides — long-thin uses 条, flat-rectangular uses 张

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 鱼 (one fish)
exercises.explanation: Fish are long and slender → 条. 一 条 鱼.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 三 ___ 票 (three tickets)
exercises.explanation: Tickets are flat sheets → 张. 三 张 票.

exercises.prompt: Match the noun to its measure word
Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 路 (one road)
exercises.explanation: Roads are long and linear → 条. 一 条 路.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 两 ___ 床 (two beds)
exercises.explanation: Beds are flat / broad surface → 张. 两 张 床.

exercises.prompt: Match noun → MW
Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 围巾 (one scarf)
exercises.explanation: Scarves are long thin strips → 条. 一 条 围巾.

exercises.prompt: Trap: which MW DOESN'T fit "long, thin things"?
exercises.explanation: Paper is flat → 张 纸, not 条 纸. (Note: a long strip torn from paper could be 一 条, but for a sheet use 张.)

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW for "a long bench (long thin furniture)": 一 ___ 长椅
exercises.explanation: Long thin bench → 条. (A regular flat seat could use 张, but a long bench is shape-长.)

exercises.prompt: Match noun → MW

pairs.left: 裙子? (no — 件) — pants 裤子

exercises.prompt: Translate 我 有 三 本 书 to natural English
exercises.explanation: Chinese has no plural -s, so English-L1 learners coming back from heavy MW practice sometimes forget plural marking. "three books" — count nouns with a number need -s.

lessons.title: 只 — animals & pairs
lessons.description: 只 for most animals and one-of-a-pair; 双 for a pair

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 猫 (one cat)
exercises.explanation: Most animals → 只. 一 只 猫.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 两 ___ 鞋 (two shoes — i.e. two singles)
exercises.explanation: Each shoe is one of a pair → 只. 一 双 鞋 = one pair; 一 只 鞋 = one (single) shoe.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 鞋 (one PAIR of shoes)
exercises.explanation: 双 = a pair. Compare 一 只 鞋 (one single shoe) vs 一 双 鞋 (one pair).

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 鸟 (one bird)
exercises.explanation: Birds use 只 — most small/medium animals do.

exercises.prompt: "她 有 一 ___ 手 很 漂亮" — pick the right MW
exercises.explanation: Hands come as a pair → 双 手 = (a pair of) hands.

exercises.prompt: Trap: pick the WRONG MW for animals
exercises.explanation: Don't use 个 for birds. 鸟 takes 只. (Dogs accept BOTH 只 and 条 — long thin dogs lean 条.)

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 筷子 (one pair of chopsticks)
exercises.explanation: Chopsticks come as a pair → 双. One single chopstick (rare!) would be 一 只 筷子.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "我 家 有 三 ___ 猫" (My family has three cats)
exercises.explanation: 三 只 猫 — animals take 只.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 两 ___ 眼睛 (two eyes)
exercises.explanation: Each eye is one of a pair → 只 眼睛 (two singles). A pair → 一 双 眼睛.

exercises.prompt: Which is the natural way to say "a pair of socks"?
exercises.explanation: Pairs (shoes, socks, gloves, chopsticks, hands, eyes) → 双. Single sock → 只.

Build "There are five birds in the tree"

lessons.title: 件 — events & clothing
lessons.description: 件 for clothes (jacket, shirt) and abstract matters (一件事 = one thing/matter)

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 衬衫 (one shirt)
exercises.explanation: Most clothing items → 件. 一 件 衬衫.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 事 (one matter / one thing to discuss)
exercises.explanation: Abstract events / matters → 件. 一 件 事 = one matter. (一 个 事 sounds wrong.)

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "我 想 告诉 你 一 ___ 事" (I want to tell you one thing)
exercises.explanation: 件 事 = matter. Set phrase.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 三 ___ 外套 (three jackets)
exercises.explanation: Jackets, coats, shirts, dresses → 件.

exercises.prompt: Trap: which clothing item does NOT take 件?
exercises.explanation: Pants → 条 (long thin shape). Tops and jackets → 件. 一 条 裤子, 一 件 毛衣.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "昨天 发生 了 一 ___ 大 事" (Yesterday a big thing happened)
exercises.explanation: Events / matters take 件. 一 件 大 事 = a big deal / important matter.

exercises.prompt: "He told me three ___" → 他 告诉 了 我 三 ___ 事
exercises.explanation: 三 件 事 = three matters / things to mention.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 这 ___ 工作 很 难 (this job is hard)
exercises.explanation: Jobs / tasks → 件 (treated as a matter). 一 件 工作.

exercises.prompt: Match noun → MW
English-L1 trap: which is WRONG?
exercises.explanation: Pens take 支 (zhī, for thin sticks) or 个 (casual). 件 is for clothing and matters, not stationery.

lessons.title: 把 / 颗 / 杯 / 瓶
lessons.description: 把 hand-held, 颗 small round, 杯 cups, 瓶 bottles

exercises.prompt: Match noun → MW
Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 椅子 (one chair)
exercises.explanation: Chairs have a back you grab → 把 (hand-held / has a handle). 一 把 椅子.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 雨伞 (one umbrella)
exercises.explanation: Umbrellas have a handle → 把. 一 把 雨伞.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 三 ___ 牙齿 (three teeth)
exercises.explanation: Small round things → 颗. 三 颗 牙齿.

exercises.prompt: Match noun → MW
Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 心 (one heart, metaphor)
exercises.explanation: Heart is treated as a small round 'precious' object → 一 颗 心. Common in song lyrics and idioms.

exercises.prompt: Fill in: "我 喝 了 两 ___ 咖啡" (I drank two cups of coffee)
exercises.explanation: 杯 = cup of. 两 杯 咖啡.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 红酒 (one BOTTLE of red wine)
exercises.explanation: 瓶 = bottle. One glass would be 一 杯; one bottle is 一 瓶.

exercises.prompt: Match noun → MW
Trap: which is WRONG?
exercises.explanation: Teeth are small + round → 颗, not 把. 把 is for hand-held things with a handle (knives, chairs, umbrellas).

lessons.title: Picking the right MW
lessons.description: Given a noun, pick its MW. English-L1 over-uses 个 — train the reflex.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 鱼
exercises.explanation: Fish are long-thin → 条. 个 is the lazy English-L1 fallback.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 大 事 (one big deal)
exercises.explanation: Matters / events → 件. (一 个 大 事 sounds wrong to natives.)

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 三 ___ 票
exercises.explanation: Tickets are flat → 张. Avoid 一 个 票.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 雨伞
exercises.explanation: Umbrella has a handle → 把. 一 个 雨伞 is the over-应用 trap.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 两 ___ 鸟
exercises.explanation: Animals → 只 by default. (Many native speakers correct learners on 一 个 鸟.)

exercises.prompt: Trap: which is the most natural?
exercises.explanation: Clothing tops → 件. 一 个 衬衫 sounds learner-y.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 三 ___ 珍珠 (three pearls)
exercises.explanation: Small round → 颗. (个 fits in casual speech but loses precision.)

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 啤酒 (one bottle of beer)
exercises.explanation: Bottle → 瓶. (A glass would be 一 杯 啤酒.)

exercises.prompt: Pick the right MW: 一 ___ 路 (one road)
exercises.explanation: Long linear shape → 条. 一 个 路 is wrong.

exercises.prompt: Trap: pick the WRONG choice (English-L1 over-uses 个)
exercises.explanation: Fish → 条, not 个. The other three are correct: 件 事, 只 猫, 张 桌子.

topics.title: Opinions & agreement
topics.description: I think, I believe, I agree — saying what you reckon

guide.intro: B1 means saying more than "I like" or "I want". You need ways to express opinions softly, agree, disagree, and ask people what THEY think. Three verbs do the heavy lifting: 觉得, 认为, and 看.

sections.text: 觉得 — feel / think (everyday)
觉得 (jué de) is the workhorse — "I feel / think that...". Use it for any soft, personal opinion. By far the most common in conversation.

rows.source: 我 觉得 这 个 电影 很 好。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhè ge diànyǐng hěn hǎo.
rows.translation: I think this movie is good.

rows.source: 你 觉得 怎么样？
rows.translation: What do you think?

sections.text: 认为 — believe / hold (more formal)
认为 (rèn wéi) is firmer and more written — "I hold the view that...". Right for opinions on bigger issues, news, business, debate.

rows.source: 我 认为 这 个 计划 不 行。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ rènwéi zhè ge jìhuà bù xíng.
rows.translation: I don't think this plan will work.

rows.source: 专家 认为 经济 会 好转。
rows.translation: Experts believe the economy will improve.

sections.text: 看 — see / view (informal opinion ask)
看 (kàn) literally means "look", but "你 看 …" idiomatically means "in your view, …". Used to gently ask someone's take.

rows.source: 你 看 我 该 怎么 办？
rows.pinyin: Nǐ kàn wǒ gāi zěnme bàn?
rows.translation: What do you think I should do?

rows.source: 我 看 应该 没 问题。
rows.translation: I think it should be fine.

sections.text: Agreeing & disagreeing
Chinese conversation tends to soften disagreement. "我 不 太 同意" (I don't really agree) is gentler and more common than a flat "不 同意".

lessons.title: I think (觉得)
lessons.description: Soft personal opinions

exercises.prompt: What does "我 觉得" (wǒ juéde) mean?
Build "I think this movie is very good"
exercises.answer: 我 觉得 这 个 电影 很 好

exercises.prompt: How do you ask "What do you think?"
options: 你 觉得 怎么样
exercises.answer: 你 觉得 怎么样

exercises.prompt: Build "I think his Chinese is pretty good"
exercises.answer: 我 觉得 他 的 中文 还 不错
exercises.explanation: 还 不错 — "pretty good / not bad". A B1 staple, milder than 很 好.

exercises.prompt: "我 觉得 这 个 价格 太 贵 了"
options: I think this price is too expensive
I'm willing to pay this price
This price is fine for me
exercises.answer: I think this price is too expensive

exercises.prompt: the soft-opinion phrase

pairs.left: 我 觉得 还 行
我 觉得 不 太 好
pairs.right: I don't really think it's good

pairs.left: 我 觉得 挺 好 的
我 觉得 没 问题

exercises.prompt: Fill: "你 ___ 这 个 计划 怎么样？" ("What do you think of this plan?")
Build "I felt the movie was a little long"
exercises.answer: 我 觉得 那 个 电影 有点 长
exercises.explanation: 有点 + adjective — "a little (negative tinge)". 有点 长 = a bit too long.

exercises.prompt: How do you politely disagree with someone's opinion using 觉得?
options: 我 觉得 不 是 这 样
Both work but the second is more natural
exercises.answer: Both work but the second is more natural
exercises.explanation: 我 不 觉得 ... is grammatical but blunt. 我 觉得 不 是 这 样 ("I don't think that's the case") softens the disagreement.

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
Translate 我 觉得 他 是 对 的 — pick the natural English
options: I feel that he is true
I felt he was the right
exercises.explanation: 觉得 in opinion contexts is "think", not "feel". "I feel he is right" sounds emotional / hesitant. Also: 对 = "right/correct" (not "true").

exercises.prompt: Build "I think you're right"
exercises.answer: 我 觉得 你 是 对 的

exercises.prompt: Fill: "我 ___ 这 个 想法 很 好" (everyday opinion verb)
"我 觉得 还 行" — what level of opinion is this?
Build "I think this plan is a bit complicated"
exercises.answer: 我 觉得 这 个 计划 有点 复杂

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
Which is a soft positive opinion?
options: 我 觉得 挺 好 的
我 觉得 不 好
我 觉得 太 贵 了
exercises.answer: 我 觉得 挺 好 的

exercises.prompt: Build "What do you think of this price?"
exercises.answer: 你 觉得 这 个 价格 怎么样

exercises.prompt: Fill: "我 觉得 没 ___" ("no problem")
"我 觉得 那 个 电影 有点 长"
options: I felt the movie was a bit long
I really liked the long movie
I want to watch a long movie
exercises.answer: I felt the movie was a bit long

lessons.title: I believe (认为)
lessons.description: Firmer, more formal opinions

exercises.prompt: How does "认为" differ from "觉得"?
options: 认为 is firmer / more formal; 觉得 is everyday
认为 only goes in questions
exercises.answer: 认为 is firmer / more formal; 觉得 is everyday

exercises.prompt: Build "I don't think this plan will work"
exercises.answer: 我 认为 这 个 计划 不 行

exercises.prompt: "专家 认为" means "___ believe"
Build "I believe this is a chance worth trying"
exercises.answer: 我 认为 这 是 一 个 值得 试 一 试 的 机会
exercises.explanation: 值得 + V + 一 + V — "worth Ving once / worth a V". B1 idiom for evaluating chances.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right register: a news article on the economy
options: 经济 学家 觉得 经济 会 好转
经济 学家 认为 经济 会 好转
经济 学家 看 经济 会 好转
经济 学家 想 经济 会 好转
exercises.answer: 经济 学家 认为 经济 会 好转
exercises.explanation: 认为 is the formal/written verb. 觉得 sounds too colloquial for news.

exercises.prompt: the 觉得 / 认为 to the right context

pairs.left: 我 觉得 这 个 菜 好 吃
专家 认为 这 个 政策 不 行
我 觉得 你 应该 休息
学者 认为 这 是 历史 事件

exercises.prompt: Fill: "老板 ___ 这 个 项目 应该 取消" (firmer opinion verb)
"我 不 认为 他 是 对 的"
exercises.explanation: 我 不 认为 — direct, formal. Stronger than 我 觉得 不 ...

exercises.prompt: Build "Many people believe traveling is a kind of education"
exercises.answer: 很 多 人 认为 旅行 是 一 种 教育

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
Which best matches "In my view, the climate is changing"?
options: 我 觉得 气候 在 变化
我 认为 气候 在 变化
我 看 气候 在 变化
Any of these work in different registers
exercises.answer: Any of these work in different registers
exercises.explanation: All three opinion verbs work; 认为 is firmest, 觉得 most casual, 看 most idiomatic.

exercises.prompt: Build "I believe this is a good chance"
exercises.answer: 我 认为 这 是 一 个 好 机会

exercises.prompt: Fill: "学者 ___ 这 是 历史 事件" (formal opinion verb)
Which register is "认为" most associated with?
Build "Experts believe the climate is changing"
exercises.answer: 专家 认为 气候 在 变化

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
"我 不 认为 这 个 计划 行"
options: I don't think this plan works
I'm not sure about the plan
exercises.answer: I don't think this plan works

exercises.prompt: Build "Many people believe travel is a kind of education"
exercises.answer: 很 多 人 认为 旅行 是 一 种 教育

exercises.prompt: Fill: "老板 ___ 项目 应该 取消" (firmer opinion verb)
Which pair shows the same meaning in different registers?

lessons.title: Agree & disagree
lessons.description: 同意, 不同意, and softer versions

exercises.prompt: the phrase
Which softens disagreement?
options: 我 不 太 同意
我 完全 不 同意
我 觉得 不 对
exercises.answer: 我 不 太 同意
exercises.explanation: 不 太 (not very) is the standard softener — politer than a flat "不".

exercises.prompt: Build "You're right, this makes sense"
exercises.answer: 你 说 得 对 ， 这 很 有 道理

exercises.prompt: "我 完全 同意 你"
Build "Sorry, I really can't agree"
exercises.answer: 对不起 我 实在 不 能 同意
exercises.explanation: 实在 (shí zài) — "really, honestly". Politely strengthens disagreement.

exercises.prompt: Fill: "这 个 想法 ___ 道理" ("makes sense" — verb that means 'has')
the response to its strength

pairs.left: 我 也 这么 想
我 不 太 同意
我 完全 不 同意

exercises.prompt: Pick the politest disagreement:
options: 你 说 得 不 对
我 觉得 不 一定 是 这 样
不 是 这 样
exercises.answer: 我 觉得 不 一定 是 这 样
exercises.explanation: 我 觉得 不 一定 ... — "I think it's not necessarily ...". Hedge, hedge, hedge.

exercises.prompt: Build "Both views make sense"
exercises.answer: 两 种 看法 都 有 道理

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
What does "我 同意 你 的 看法 ， 不过 ..." signal?
options: Polite agreement followed by a counterpoint
exercises.answer: Polite agreement followed by a counterpoint
exercises.explanation: 不过 = "however / but". Standard "yes, but ..." Chinese debate move.

exercises.prompt: Build "I also think so"
exercises.answer: 我 也 这么 想

exercises.prompt: Fill: "我 ___ 同意 你" ("completely")
Which means "it makes sense"?
Build "I don't really think it's a good idea"
exercises.answer: 我 不 太 觉得 这 是 个 好 主意

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
"我 同意 你 的 看法 ， 不过 ..." — what's the move here?
options: Mild agreement with a coming caveat
exercises.answer: Mild agreement with a coming caveat

exercises.prompt: Build "Sorry, I disagree"
exercises.answer: 对不起 我 不 同意

exercises.prompt: Fill: "两 ___ 看法 都 有 道理" ("kinds of")
Which is the strongest disagreement?
options: 不 一定 是 这样

lessons.title: Asking for opinions
lessons.description: 你看 / 你怎么想

exercises.prompt: What does "你 看 我 该 怎么 办？" mean?
options: What do you think I should do?
exercises.answer: What do you think I should do?

exercises.prompt: Build "I think it should be fine"
exercises.answer: 我 看 应该 没 问题

exercises.prompt: Tap the question you hear
Build "What's your view on this issue?"
exercises.answer: 你 对 这 个 问题 怎么 看
exercises.explanation: 对 X 怎么 看 — "how do you see / view X". The pattern that turns 看 into the opinion verb.

exercises.prompt: "我 看 不 行"
exercises.explanation: 我 看 + assertion = "as I see it". Idiomatic; nothing to do with literal vision.

exercises.prompt: the way to ask for an opinion

pairs.left: 你 觉得 怎么样

pairs.right: How do you feel about it?

pairs.left: 你 的 看法 是 什么

exercises.prompt: Fill: "你 ___ 这 件 事 怎么 看" ("toward / about")
Pick the most natural way to ask a friend's casual take:
options: 您 对 此 有 何 看法
请问 您 的 高 见
exercises.explanation: 你 看 呢 — short, casual, friend-to-friend. The other options are formal/written/honorific.

exercises.prompt: Build "In your view, which restaurant is better?"
exercises.answer: 你 看 哪 家 餐厅 比较 好

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
"我 觉得 应该 没 什么 问题"
options: I think there should be no problem
I don't think there's a problem
All of the above are reasonable in context
exercises.answer: All of the above are reasonable in context
exercises.explanation: "应该 没 什么 问题" is hedging — "probably no issue". Translation depends on context.

exercises.prompt: Build "What's your view?"
exercises.answer: 你 的 看法 是 什么

exercises.prompt: Fill: "你 看 我 ___ 怎么 办" ("should")
Which means "I think it should be fine"?
options: 我 看 应该 没 问题
我 看 有 问题
我 不 看 问题
exercises.answer: 我 看 应该 没 问题

exercises.prompt: Build "In your view, which one is better?"
exercises.answer: 你 看 哪 个 比较 好

exercises.prompt: Tap what you hear
"我 看 不 行" — what does the speaker think?
options: The speaker thinks it won't work
The speaker doesn't want to look
exercises.answer: The speaker thinks it won't work

exercises.prompt: Build "How do you see this issue?"
exercises.answer: 你 对 这 个 问题 怎么 看

exercises.prompt: Fill: "你 ___ 这 件 事 怎么 看" ("toward / about")
Which is the most casual way to ask a friend's take?
options: 请问 您 的 高 见
您 对 此 有 何 看法

topics.title: Telling a story
topics.description: Sequencing past events with 着 and directional verbs

guide.intro: When you narrate a story you need ways to set the scene ("she was sitting"), describe motion ("he walked in"), and string events together. 着 handles ongoing states; directional complements like 上来 and 下去 handle motion in space.

sections.text: 着 — ongoing state
着 (zhe) attached to a verb means "in the state of doing". It's NOT the same as English -ing — 着 emphasizes a held position or background condition, often setting the scene.

rows.translation: He is standing. (in a standing state)
The door is open. (held open)

rows.source: 她 笑 着 说。
rows.translation: She said with a smile. (smiling-while-speaking)

sections.text: 着 vs 在: 在 means "actively doing right now" ("我 在 吃饭" — I'm eating). 着 means "in this state" ("门 开 着" — the door's open). For narration, 着 sets the scene; 在 reports a live action.
Directional complements: 上 / 下 / 进 / 出 / 来 / 去
Six little words combine into rich verbs of motion. Pair a base direction (up/down/in/out) with 来 (toward speaker) or 去 (away from speaker).

rows.source: 他 走 进来 了。
rows.translation: He walked in.

rows.source: 她 跑 出去 了。
rows.translation: She ran out.
Please come up.

sections.text: Figurative directionals — 起来 / 下去 / 出来
Directional complements stretch beyond physical motion. Attached to non-motion verbs, they signal phase or aspect: starting, continuing, or coming-to-clarity.

rows: 看 起来 很 累 — looks tired

rows.source: 我 终于 想 出来 了。
rows.translation: I finally figured it out.

rows.source: 请 你 说 下 去。
rows.translation: Please keep talking.

rows.source: 他 突然 笑 起来 了。
rows.translation: He suddenly started to laugh.

sections.text: Sequencing words
A2's 然后 still works, but B1 stories add 先...再... (first...then...), 最后 (finally), 突然 (suddenly), and 后来 (afterward — for events further apart).

rows.source: 我 先 吃饭，再 看 电影。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ xiān chīfàn, zài kàn diànyǐng.
rows.translation: First I'll eat, then watch a movie.
It suddenly started to rain.

rows.source: 后来 他 搬 走 了。
rows.translation: Afterward, he moved away.

levels.name: B2 — Upper Intermediate
levels.description: Discuss abstract topics, defend opinions, and handle the news, the workplace, and contemporary Chinese culture.

topics.title: Expressing opinions
topics.description: Hedge, agree, push back, and stack reasons

guide.intro: At B2 you stop just stating opinions and start structuring them — adding nuance, layering reasons, and naming the side you fall on. Three patterns will carry most of your opinion-talk for the rest of your Chinese life: 不仅…而且 (not only…but also), 我觉得…比较 (I think…relatively), and 一方面…另一方面 (on one hand…on the other).

sections.text: 不仅…而且 — not only…but also

不仅 (bù jǐn) sets up the first half of a two-part claim, and 而且 (ér qiě) adds the second, usually stronger, point. The two halves can share a subject (which sits in front) or have different subjects (which sit after each particle).

rows.source: 他不仅会说中文，而且会说日语。
rows.pinyin: Tā bù jǐn huì shuō Zhōngwén, ér qiě huì shuō Rìyǔ.
rows.translation: He not only speaks Chinese, but also Japanese.

rows.source: 这家餐厅不仅便宜，而且很好吃。
rows.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng bù jǐn piányi, ér qiě hěn hǎo chī.
rows.translation: This restaurant is not only cheap but also delicious.

rows.source: 不仅我喜欢他，而且我妹妹也喜欢他。
rows.pinyin: Bù jǐn wǒ xǐhuan tā, ér qiě wǒ mèimei yě xǐhuan tā.
rows.translation: Not only do I like him, but my sister does too.

sections.text: Common mistake: dropping 而且 and joining with a comma. In Mandarin, 不仅 always pairs with 而且 (or 也 / 还). "他不仅高，帅" sounds incomplete.
Softening: 我觉得 + 比较

比较 (bǐ jiào) means "relatively" or "fairly" — it takes the edge off an opinion the way "kind of" does in English. Pair it with 我觉得 (wǒ jué de, "I feel") for a polite, hedged tone that won't sound confrontational.

rows.source: 我觉得这个想法比较有意思。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ jué de zhè ge xiǎngfǎ bǐ jiào yǒu yì si.
rows.translation: I think this idea is fairly interesting.

rows.source: 我觉得他说的比较有道理。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ jué de tā shuō de bǐ jiào yǒu dào lǐ.
rows.translation: I think what he said makes a fair amount of sense.

sections.text: Two sides: 一方面…另一方面
Use 一方面 (yī fāng miàn)…另一方面 (lìng yī fāng miàn) to lay out two sides of the same issue — the closest Mandarin gets to "on one hand…on the other hand".

rows.source: 一方面工作很累，另一方面工资也不高。
rows.pinyin: Yī fāng miàn gōng zuò hěn lèi, lìng yī fāng miàn gōng zī yě bù gāo.
rows.translation: On one hand the work is tiring, on the other hand the pay isn't great either.

exercises.prompt: Yesterday I read this article. Pick the natural Mandarin order — time word placement:
exercises.explanation: In Chinese, time words go before the verb — usually at the start of the clause or right after the subject. "我看了这篇文章昨天" (English order) is wrong.

exercises.prompt: English: "Because the movie was long, so I left." In Chinese, picking BOTH 因为 and 所以 is fine. But which natural rendering matches B2 register?
options: 因为电影太长了，所以我就走了。
因为电影太长了，我就走了所以。
我走了所以因为电影太长。
电影太长所以因为我走了。
exercises.answer: 因为电影太长了，所以我就走了。
exercises.explanation: Unlike English, where doubling "because…so" sounds redundant, Chinese commonly uses both 因为…所以…together. Just keep them at the start of each clause.

exercises.source: 我个人认为这个想法值得考虑
exercises.answer: Personally I believe this idea is worth considering
acceptableAnswers: I personally believe this idea deserves consideration
In my personal view this idea is worth thinking about
exercises.explanation: 我个人认为 lifts the register from casual 我觉得 — common in essays and meetings.

exercises.prompt: Build "In my view, this view is not entirely correct"
exercises.answer: 在 我 看 来 这 个 看法 不 完全 正确

exercises.prompt: Pick the most hedged way to say "I think it's a bit expensive":
exercises.explanation: 有点儿 + adj is the classic hedge. The other options are blunt/casual.

exercises.prompt: Lift the register: casual 我觉得 → formal/considered "我 ___ 这个想法很好"
exercises.explanation: 认为 is the considered/formal cousin of 觉得.

exercises.source: 我觉得他说的比较有道理
exercises.answer: I think what he said makes fairly good sense
acceptableAnswers: I feel he has a fairly reasonable point
I think what he says is fairly reasonable

exercises.prompt: Tap the opener you hear
exercises.spokenText: 我 个 人 认 为
options: 我 个 人 认 为
我 个 人 觉 得
我 在 看 来
依 我 之 见
exercises.answer: 我 个 人 认 为
exercises.explanation: 我个人认为 — five syllables, formal opener. Listen for the 4-tone 认 and 2-tone 为.

lessons.title: Not only, but also
lessons.description: Stack reasons with 不仅…而且

exercises.prompt: Build "This restaurant is not only cheap but also delicious"
exercises.answer: 这家 餐厅 不仅 便宜 而且 很 好吃

exercises.prompt: Pick the best translation for "Not only do I like him, my sister also likes him":
options: 不仅我喜欢他，而且我妹妹也喜欢他
exercises.answer: 不仅我喜欢他，而且我妹妹也喜欢他

exercises.source: 他不仅聪明，而且很努力
exercises.answer: He is not only smart but also hardworking
acceptableAnswers: Not only is he smart, he is also hardworking
He's not only clever but also diligent

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: 不仅 must pair with 而且 / 还 / 也. A bare comma is not enough — the second clause needs a connector.

exercises.prompt: 不仅 cannot pair with which of these?
exercises.explanation: 但是 introduces contrast ("but"). 不仅 needs an additive partner: 而且, 还, or 也.

exercises.prompt: Convert single-clause to compound: "He's hardworking and talented" → use 不仅...而且
exercises.answer: 他 不仅 努力 而且 有 才华

exercises.prompt: "这部电影不仅好看，___ 很有意义"
exercises.explanation: Any of 而且 / 还 / 也 completes the 不仅 pattern. The most common written choice is 而且.

exercises.prompt: Build "This phone is not only expensive but also doesn't have a good battery"
exercises.answer: 这 部 手机 不仅 贵 而且 电池 也 不 好

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "Not only does she sing, she also dances":
options: 她不仅会唱歌，还会跳舞
exercises.answer: 她不仅会唱歌，还会跳舞

exercises.source: 内卷不仅影响年轻人，还影响整个社会
exercises.answer: Involution doesn't only affect young people, it also affects the whole society
acceptableAnswers: Involution affects not only young people but the whole society
Not only does involution affect young people, it affects all of society
exercises.explanation: 内卷 — the cutthroat competition meme. The 不仅...还 frame stacks two scopes of impact.

exercises.prompt: Tap the connector you hear
exercises.explanation: 不仅 (bù jǐn) and 不但 (bù dàn) are near-synonyms — 不但 is slightly more spoken. 不过 means "however" and 不然 means "otherwise". Listen for the second syllable.

exercises.prompt: Build "He's not only smart, but also very hardworking"
exercises.answer: 他 不仅 聪明 而且 非常 努力

exercises.prompt: 不仅 cannot pair with:
exercises.explanation: 可是 introduces contrast. 不仅 needs an additive: 而且 / 还 / 也.

exercises.source: 他不仅会说中文，还会说日语
exercises.answer: He not only speaks Chinese, but also Japanese
acceptableAnswers: Not only does he speak Chinese, he speaks Japanese too
He can speak Chinese as well as Japanese

exercises.prompt: "这家餐厅 ___ 便宜，___ 很好吃"
exercises.explanation: Classic 不仅...而且 frame for stacking two positive points.

exercises.prompt: Build "Not only do I like him, but my sister also likes him"
exercises.answer: 不仅 我 喜欢 他 而且 我 妹妹 也 喜欢 他

exercises.prompt: Best translation: "This restaurant is not only cheap but also delicious":
options: 这家餐厅不仅便宜而且很好吃
exercises.answer: 这家餐厅不仅便宜而且很好吃
He is not only tall but also very handsome
acceptableAnswers: Not only is he tall, he is also very handsome
He's tall and also very good-looking

exercises.prompt: Build "Involution not only affects work, but also affects life"
exercises.answer: 内卷 不仅 影响 工作 还 影响 生活

exercises.prompt: Tap the second-half connector you hear
exercises.explanation: 而且 (ér qiě) is the standard partner of 不仅. Don't confuse with 但是 (contrast).

lessons.title: Agree & disagree
lessons.description: 同意, 反对, and the polite middle

exercises.prompt: the phrase to its meaning
Which is the most polite way to disagree?
exercises.explanation: Literally "I have a different view" — softer than a direct "you're wrong".

exercises.prompt: Build "I basically agree with your point of view"
exercises.answer: 我 基本 同意 你 的 看法

exercises.prompt: the agreement to its strength

pairs.right: Soft: I feel that way too

exercises.prompt: the disagreement to its tone

pairs.right: Pushback: I wouldn't put it that way

exercises.prompt: Build a hedged disagreement: "I'm not entirely sure I agree with this view"
exercises.answer: 我 不 太 确定 我 同意 这 个 看法

exercises.prompt: Your boss states a view in a meeting. Which response is appropriate?
options: 您的看法很有道理，不过我有一点不同意见
exercises.answer: 您的看法很有道理，不过我有一点不同意见
exercises.explanation: Concede first (有道理), then introduce disagreement with 不过 ("however") and a softener like 一点 — the standard formula for pushback in formal settings.
话是这么说，可是… is the most common spoken way to concede a point and pivot to your real objection.

exercises.prompt: Pick the strongest agreement:
Build a hedge: "To some extent, I agree with you"
exercises.answer: 在 某 种 程度 上 我 同意 你
exercises.explanation: 在某种程度上 — "to a certain degree" — the classic essay hedge before partial agreement.

exercises.prompt: Tap the phrase you hear
exercises.spokenText: 我 不 太 同意
options: 我 不 太 同意
exercises.answer: 我 不 太 同意
exercises.explanation: 不太 + verb is the soft-disagreement frame. Hear it as a polite "not quite" rather than "not at all".

exercises.prompt: Build "I completely agree with your view"
exercises.answer: 我 完全 同意 你 的 看法

exercises.prompt: Pick the polite pushback for use with a boss:
options: 您说得有道理，不过我有一点不同看法
exercises.answer: 您说得有道理，不过我有一点不同看法
exercises.explanation: Concede first (有道理), then introduce disagreement softly (一点不同看法).

exercises.answer: I basically agree with your view
acceptableAnswers: I largely agree with your view
I mostly agree with what you think

exercises.prompt: Soft pushback: "我 ___ 同意你的看法" (I don't quite agree)
exercises.explanation: 不太 + verb is the soft-disagreement frame: "not quite agree" instead of "disagree".

exercises.prompt: Build "To some extent, what you said makes sense"
exercises.answer: 在 某 种 程度 上 你 说 得 有 道理

exercises.prompt: Which phrase is the strongest disagreement?
exercises.explanation: 完全反对 = completely opposed. The others are all softened/polite forms.

exercises.answer: I wouldn't put it that way
acceptableAnswers: You can't say it like that
That's not quite how I'd put it
exercises.context: huà bù néng zhè me shuō

exercises.prompt: Build "That's indeed the case, but…"
exercises.answer: 确实 如此 但是

exercises.prompt: Tap the strong-agreement phrase you hear
exercises.spokenText: 完 全 同 意
options: 完 全 同 意
基 本 同 意
不 太 同 意
完 全 反 对
exercises.answer: 完 全 同 意
exercises.explanation: 完全同意 — "completely agree". The strongest form on the agreement spectrum.

lessons.title: Two sides of an issue
lessons.description: 一方面…另一方面 and 既…又

exercises.prompt: What does "一方面…另一方面" mean?
options: On one hand… on the other hand
exercises.answer: On one hand… on the other hand

exercises.prompt: Build "On one hand the work is tiring, on the other hand the pay isn't high"
exercises.answer: 一方面 工作 很 累 另一方面 工资 也 不 高
She is both smart and beautiful
acceptableAnswers: She is smart as well as beautiful
exercises.explanation: 既…又 (jì…yòu) stacks two qualities of the same subject — "both…and".

exercises.prompt: Which best translates "It's expensive but worth it"?
Build "On one hand the salary is high, on the other hand the pressure is also great"
exercises.answer: 一方面 工资 很 高 另一方面 压力 也 很 大

exercises.source: 这个工作既稳定又有意思
exercises.answer: This job is both stable and interesting
acceptableAnswers: This job is stable and also interesting
It's a job that is both steady and interesting
exercises.explanation: 既...又 — stacks two qualities of one subject. 既 X 又 Y means "both X and Y".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: 既 pairs with 又 (not 也). 既 X 又 Y is the locked frame.

exercises.prompt: Build "Studying abroad has both advantages and disadvantages"
exercises.answer: 出国 留学 既 有 好处 又 有 坏处

exercises.prompt: the two-sided pattern

pairs.right: On one hand…on the other (separate clauses)

acceptableAnswers: There are two sides to everything
exercises.context: fán shì dōu yǒu liǎng miàn
exercises.explanation: A common B2 set phrase to open a balanced opinion. 凡事 = every matter.

exercises.prompt: Build "Although AI is convenient, it also brings problems"
exercises.answer: 虽然 人工智能 很 方便 但是 也 带 来 一些 问题

exercises.prompt: Pick the most balanced essay-style opening:
options: 凡事都有两面：一方面…另一方面…
exercises.answer: 凡事都有两面：一方面…另一方面…
exercises.explanation: Balanced essays in Chinese almost always open with 凡事都有两面 or a similar two-sides formula before laying out 一方面 / 另一方面.

exercises.source: 一方面工作很累，另一方面工资也不高
exercises.answer: On one hand the work is tiring, on the other hand the pay isn't high either
acceptableAnswers: On one hand work is exhausting; on the other, the pay is also not high
The work is tiring, and the pay isn't great either

exercises.prompt: Build "This restaurant is both cheap and delicious" (既...又)
exercises.answer: 这家 餐厅 既 便宜 又 好吃

exercises.prompt: 既 must pair with which word?
exercises.explanation: 既 X 又 Y is locked. 也 pairs with 不仅, not 既.

exercises.prompt: "一方面 工资 很 高 ___ 压力 也 很 大"
exercises.explanation: 一方面 must pair with 另一方面 — the locked two-sides frame.

exercises.answer: She is both pretty and smart
acceptableAnswers: She is both beautiful and clever
She's pretty as well as smart

exercises.prompt: Build "Everything has two sides — one hand the advantages, on the other the disadvantages"
exercises.answer: 凡事 都 有 两 面 一方面 好处 另一方面 坏处

exercises.prompt: Pick the GRAMMATICALLY CORRECT sentence:
options: 这个工作既稳定又有意思
这个工作既稳定也有意思
一方面工作很累也另一方面工资不高
exercises.answer: 这个工作既稳定又有意思
exercises.explanation: 既 must pair with 又, not 也 / 但是. 一方面 must pair with 另一方面.

exercises.prompt: Tap the two-sided opener you hear
options: 另 一 方 面
凡 事 两 面
一 方 二 面
exercises.explanation: 一方面 (yī fāng miàn) — "on one hand". Three syllables, falling-rising-falling cadence.

lessons.title: Dialogue: Discussing a film at a coffee shop
lessons.description: Hedge your film opinions, half-agree, and recommend with a caveat

exercises.prompt: Coffee-shop chat about a film you saw last night

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 你昨天看的那部电影怎么样？(Nǐ zuótiān kàn de nà bù diànyǐng zěnmeyàng?)
turns.spokenText: 你昨天看的那部电影怎么样？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Soften your opinion (hedging).
options: 我觉得剧情比较拖沓，不过演技不错。(Wǒ juéde jùqíng bǐjiào tuōtà, búguò yǎnjì búcuò.)
剧情绝对烂透了，没什么好说的。(Jùqíng juéduì làn tòule, méi shénme hǎo shuō de.)
电影虽然好，因此结尾差。(Diànyǐng suīrán hǎo, yīncǐ jiéwěi chà.)
turns.answer: 我觉得剧情比较拖沓，不过演技不错。(Wǒ juéde jùqíng bǐjiào tuōtà, búguò yǎnjì búcuò.)

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 对，我也觉得节奏有点慢。(Duì, wǒ yě juéde jiézòu yǒudiǎn màn.)
turns.spokenText: 对，我也觉得节奏有点慢。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Half-agree, then add a nuance.
options: 我部分同意，不过那些慢镜头反而很有味道。(Wǒ bùfèn tóngyì, búguò nàxiē màn jìngtóu fǎn'ér hěn yǒu wèidào.)
完全同意而且非常好。(Wánquán tóngyì érqiě fēicháng hǎo.)
不知道我无所谓的吧。(Bù zhīdào wǒ wúsuǒwèi de ba.)
turns.answer: 我部分同意，不过那些慢镜头反而很有味道。(Wǒ bùfèn tóngyì, búguò nàxiē màn jìngtóu fǎn'ér hěn yǒu wèidào.)

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 说得也是。导演想表达的主题你看懂了吗？(Shuō de yěshì. Dǎoyǎn xiǎng biǎodá de zhǔtí nǐ kàndǒng le ma?)
turns.spokenText: 说得也是。导演想表达的主题你看懂了吗？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill in the hedge — 'I feel maybe'.
turns.after: 是在讲家庭的疏离感。(Wǒ ___ shì zài jiǎng jiātíng de shūlí gǎn.)
turns.answer: 觉得大概

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 嗯，那种感觉确实贯穿全片。(Èn, nà zhǒng gǎnjué quèshí guànchuān quánpiàn.)
turns.spokenText: 嗯，那种感觉确实贯穿全片。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Recommend it — but with a caveat.
options: 推荐看，不过得有耐心，节奏比较慢。(Tuījiàn kàn, búguò děi yǒu nàixīn, jiézòu bǐjiào màn.)
强烈不推荐，肯定别看了。(Qiángliè bù tuījiàn, kěndìng bié kàn le.)
可以看也可以不看反正都行。(Kěyǐ kàn yě kěyǐ bù kàn fǎnzhèng dōu xíng.)
turns.answer: 推荐看，不过得有耐心，节奏比较慢。(Tuījiàn kàn, búguò děi yǒu nàixīn, jiézòu bǐjiào màn.)

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: 好，我下周找时间去看。(Hǎo, wǒ xià zhōu zhǎo shíjiān qù kàn.)
turns.spokenText: 好，我下周找时间去看。

exercises.prompt: Which best HEDGES "I think the plot is a bit draggy"?
exercises.explanation: 比较 (relatively) softens the criticism — classic Chinese hedge.

exercises.prompt: Soften: "剧情___拖沓" (somewhat draggy)
exercises.hint: use a softener like "relatively" or "a bit"

exercises.prompt: Pick the connector for half-agreement ("I partly agree, but..."):
exercises.explanation: 部分同意 = partial agreement; 不过 introduces the nuance.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Those slow shots actually have flavor"
exercises.answer: 那些 慢镜头 反而 很 有 味道

exercises.prompt: Hedge with "maybe": "我觉得___是在讲家庭的疏离感"
What does 贯穿全片 mean?
exercises.explanation: 贯穿 = run through; 全片 = the whole film. A theme that 贯穿 the film is woven throughout it.

exercises.answer: I recommend watching it, but you need patience
acceptableAnswers: recommended, but you need to be patient
I'd recommend it, though you'll need patience

exercises.prompt: The phrase 反而 signals:

exercises.prompt: Theme runs through the film: "那种感觉确实___全片"
Tap the hedge you hear
exercises.spokenText: 我 觉 得 大 概
options: 我 觉 得 大 概
我 大 概 觉 得

觉 得 我 大 概

exercises.prompt: Build: "Recommended, but you need patience"

exercises.prompt: Which is the most natural way to recommend with a caveat?
options: 推荐看，不过节奏比较慢
推荐看因此节奏比较慢
exercises.answer: 推荐看，不过节奏比较慢

exercises.prompt: phrase to function

exercises.answer: the theme the director wants to express
acceptableAnswers: the theme the director was trying to express
the topic the director wanted to express

exercises.prompt: Recommend with caveat: "推荐看，___得有耐心"
疏离感 most accurately means:

exercises.answer: 我 部分 同意 不过 慢 节奏 反而 有 味道

穿 贯 全 片
exercises.answer: 贯 穿 全 片

topics.title: News & current events
topics.description: Read a headline, summarize what happened, give your take

lessons.title: News vocabulary
lessons.description: 新闻, 报道, 媒体 — the building blocks

exercises.prompt: the term to its meaning
What does "头条新闻" (tóu tiáo xīn wén) mean?
exercises.explanation: 头条 literally means "top entry" — but it's also the name of a hugely popular news app, 今日头条.

exercises.prompt: the news-vocabulary term
What does "自媒体" (zì méi tǐ) mean?
exercises.explanation: 自媒体 — literally "self-media". The Weibo / WeChat public accounts ecosystem; contrasted with 传统媒体 (traditional media).

exercises.prompt: online vs traditional media term
Build "This piece of news got onto the trending list (热搜)"
exercises.answer: 这 条 新闻 上 了 热搜

exercises.prompt: What does "假新闻" (jiǎ xīn wén) mean?
Build "Today's headline news is about education reform"
exercises.answer: 今天 的 头条 新闻 是 关于 教育 改革

exercises.prompt: Tap the news vocab you hear
exercises.spokenText: 突 发 新 闻
options: 突 发 新 闻
头 条 新 闻
突 然 新 闻
热 门 新 闻
exercises.answer: 突 发 新 闻
exercises.explanation: 突发 (tū fā) — "suddenly occurring" — pairs with 新闻 to form the breaking-news idiom. Don't confuse with 头条 (headline) or 突然 (suddenly).

exercises.prompt: Which is the most NEWS-REGISTER way to start a sentence?
options: 我朋友说今天那个事儿…
exercises.explanation: 据相关媒体报道 — "according to relevant media reports" — the standard news opener. The casual options would never appear in a print or anchor segment.

exercises.prompt: English speakers often drop 了 in past narration. "The earthquake happened yesterday" — which is correct?
exercises.explanation: Past completion of a specific event needs 了 after the verb. Dropping it sounds like a generic / habitual statement.

exercises.prompt: Resultative complement — "I read the article" (and finished it). Pick the natural form:
exercises.explanation: English "I read the article" implies completion, but Chinese 看 alone just means "look at". 看完 (read-finish) explicitly marks the result.

exercises.context: jù xiāng guān méi tǐ bào dào

exercises.prompt: Build "Today's breaking news is about education reform"
exercises.answer: 今天 的 突发 新闻 是 关于 教育 改革

exercises.prompt: What does "自媒体" refer to?
exercises.explanation: 自媒体 — WeChat public-account / Weibo-style independent media.

exercises.prompt: "这 条 新闻 ___ 了 热搜"
exercises.explanation: 上热搜 = make it onto the trending search list. 上 here is the verb "to ascend onto".

exercises.prompt: Tap the news term you hear
exercises.explanation: 记者 (jì zhě) — reporter. 4th tone + neutral tone. Common in news bylines.

lessons.title: What happened?
lessons.description: 发生, 引起, 影响 — narrating events

exercises.prompt: What does "发生" (fā shēng) mean?
Build "This event has had a big impact on society"
exercises.answer: 这件 事 对 社会 有 很大 的 影响

exercises.context: yǐn qǐ guǎng fàn guān zhù

exercises.prompt: What does "事故" (shì gù) mean?
the verb to its meaning
Convert active to passive: "The accident was caused by drunk driving" using 被
exercises.answer: 这 起 事故 是 由 酒驾 造成 的
exercises.explanation: News register prefers 是…由…造成的 over plain 被. 由 marks the agent. 起 is the measure word for incidents.

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "This decision will have far-reaching effects":
options: 这个决定会产生深远的影响
exercises.answer: 这个决定会产生深远的影响
exercises.explanation: 产生影响 — "produce an impact" — is the standard collocation. 深远 ("far-reaching") is essay-register.

topics.title: Environment & climate
topics.description: Pollution, recycling, climate change — and the more you do, the more it helps

guide.intro: 越…越 (yuè…yuè) is one of the most useful patterns at B2 — and one of the prettiest. It means "the more X, the more Y". You'll hear it everywhere from weather reports to op-eds. This topic uses environmental issues as the playground for it.

sections.text: 越…越 — the more…the more
The pattern is fixed: 越 + verb/adjective, 越 + verb/adjective. The two halves can share a subject (which sits at the front) or have different subjects.

rows.pinyin: Tiān qì yuè lái yuè rè.
rows.translation: The weather is getting hotter and hotter.

rows.pinyin: Tā yuè shuō yuè shēng qì.
rows.translation: The more he talked, the angrier he got.
The rain came down heavier and heavier.

sections.text: 越来越 — getting X-er
越来越 (yuè lái yuè) is the most common form: "more and more". It always sits in front of an adjective or stative verb, and signals a trend over time.

rows.pinyin: Kōng qì yuè lái yuè chà.
rows.translation: The air is getting worse and worse.

rows.pinyin: Huán bǎo yuè lái yuè zhòng yào.
rows.translation: Environmental protection is getting more and more important.

sections.text: Don't add 很 between 越来越 and the adjective. "越来越很热" is wrong — 越来越 already does the intensifying.
Two-subject form
When the two halves have different subjects, both subjects appear inside the pattern, after each 越:

rows.source: 天气越冷，我越想吃火锅。
rows.pinyin: Tiān qì yuè lěng, wǒ yuè xiǎng chī huǒ guō.
rows.translation: The colder the weather, the more I want hotpot.

topics.title: Emotions in depth
topics.description: Beyond happy and sad — frustrated, moved, embarrassed, even-if-I

guide.intro: B2 emotions need B2 grammar. The patterns 即使…也 (even if…still) and 尽管 (although) let you say things like "even if I'm tired, I'll still finish" and "although I'm sad, I'm okay" — exactly the kind of nuance you start needing once you go past 我很高兴.

sections.text: 即使…也 — even if…still

即使 (jí shǐ) introduces a hypothetical or extreme condition; the second half always uses 也 (yě, "still") or 还 (hái) to mark that the result holds regardless. Without that 也, the sentence sounds incomplete to a native ear.

rows.pinyin: Jí shǐ xià yǔ, wǒ yě yào qù.
rows.translation: Even if it rains, I'll still go.

rows.pinyin: Jí shǐ hěn lèi, tā yě bù fàng qì.
rows.translation: Even if he's tired, he doesn't give up.

rows.source: 即使没有钱，我也很快乐。
rows.pinyin: Jí shǐ méi yǒu qián, wǒ yě hěn kuài lè.
rows.translation: Even without money, I'm still happy.

sections.text: 即使 is for hypotheticals ("even if it rains") — events that may or may not happen. 即便 (jí biàn) is a slightly more formal synonym you'll see in writing.
尽管…但是 — although

尽管 (jǐn guǎn) introduces an actual fact (not a hypothetical), and 但是 (dàn shì, "but") or 还是 (hái shi, "still") marks the contrasting follow-up. Use 尽管 when the first clause is true and the second clause is the surprise.

rows.source: 尽管下雨，他还是去跑步了。
rows.pinyin: Jǐn guǎn xià yǔ, tā hái shi qù pǎo bù le.
rows.translation: Although it was raining, he still went running.

rows.source: 尽管我们很努力，但是没有成功。
rows.pinyin: Jǐn guǎn wǒ men hěn nǔ lì, dàn shì méi yǒu chéng gōng.
rows.translation: Although we tried hard, we didn't succeed.

lessons.title: Asking sharper questions

exercises.prompt: What does "难道" (nán dào) add to a question?
Build "Don't tell me you don't know?"

acceptableAnswers: How could you possibly think this way?

exercises.prompt: Tap the word you hear
exercises.explanation: 反对 (fǎn duì, "oppose") and 反应 (fǎn yìng, "reaction") share 反 but the second syllable is different — 对 is 4th tone, 应 is 4th tone but with a totally different vowel. Mishearing this in a debate is a real beginner trap.

exercises.prompt: What does "难道X不Y吗?" express?
options: A rhetorical question with disbelief — "surely X is Y?"
exercises.answer: A rhetorical question with disbelief — "surely X is Y?"
exercises.explanation: 难道 + statement + 吗 = pushy rhetorical question. 难道你不知道吗？ = "Don't tell me you don't know!" The expected answer is "of course I do".

exercises.prompt: Build a rhetorical question: "Don't you think this is unfair?"
exercises.answer: 难道 你 不 觉得 这 不 公平 吗

exercises.prompt: "哪里有这样的道理？" (nǎ lǐ yǒu zhè yàng de dào lǐ) is a ___ question.
exercises.explanation: 哪里 (nǎ lǐ) here is rhetorical, not asking "where". Means "how could there be such a logic?!" — a sharp pushback.

exercises.prompt: Best translation for "How could you say something like that?" (rhetorical):
exercises.explanation: 怎么能 — "how could (you)" — is the standard structure for outraged rhetorical questions.

exercises.prompt: Build "Why do you say it this way?"
exercises.answer: 你 为 什么 这么 说

exercises.prompt: the question type to its tone

acceptableAnswers: There's no way this is possible
exercises.context: zhè zěn me kě néng ne
exercises.explanation: 怎么可能 — incredulous protest. The 呢 at the end softens it from outrage to genuine bafflement.

exercises.prompt: Tap the rhetorical opener you hear
exercises.explanation: 难道 (nán dào) — "don't tell me that…". Don't confuse with 难怪 (no wonder), 难看 (ugly), or 难受 (uncomfortable). Listen for the 4th-tone 道.

exercises.prompt: 因为…所以… in English requires picking ONE ("because" or "so", not both). In Chinese, which is most natural?
options: 因为他不同意，所以我们没决定。
因为他不同意，我们没决定所以。
他不同意因为，我们没决定所以。
因为他不同意。我们没决定。
exercises.answer: 因为他不同意，所以我们没决定。
exercises.explanation: Chinese uses 因为…所以… as a matched pair — keeping both is standard, not redundant like in English. Position: each at the start of its clause.

exercises.prompt: 把 omission — "I sent the proposal to the boss." Most natural?
exercises.explanation: When the verb has a beneficiary (发给) + a definite object (the proposal), 把 puts the object up front and keeps the directional clear. The other orders sound off or ambiguous.

acceptableAnswers: Why would you think this way?
How could you possibly think that?

exercises.prompt: What does "难道X不Y吗?" express?
exercises.explanation: 难道 + statement + 吗 = rhetorical with disbelief.

exercises.prompt: Tap the rhetorical opener you hear
exercises.explanation: 难道 (nán dào) — "don't tell me…". 2nd tone + 4th tone.

topics.title: Formal communication
topics.description: Emails, speeches, signs — when 你 becomes 您

guide.intro: Mandarin makes a sharp distinction between casual and formal register. The same idea — "Could you please send me the document?" — sounds completely different in a WeChat to a friend versus an email to a client. B2 is where you start being able to switch.

sections.text: Pronouns and politeness

您 (nín) is the polite "you". You'll use it for clients, customers, elders, professors, and strangers in any service context. In groups, 您们 is rare — most speakers stay with 您 (singular) or use 各位 (everyone).
Word swaps that lift the register
Email openers and closers

sections.text: Casual Chinese loves 啊, 呢, 啦 — the little sentence-final particles that soften tone. Formal Chinese strips them all out. If you find yourself writing 你好啊 to a client, switch back to 您好.
Quick guide: discourse particles
Particles carry no dictionary meaning but huge emotional color. Use them in casual speech; strip them in formal writing.

items: 哎 (āi) — getting attention or expressing mild dismay: 哎，你来一下 (Hey, come here a sec)
哎呀 (āi yā) — "oh!" / "oops!" — surprise or annoyance: 哎呀，又下雨了 (Ugh, it's raining again)
啊 (a) — softens a statement or question: 你好啊 (Hi there) / 真的啊？ (Really?)
呢 (ne) — "and you?" / continuing-state marker: 你呢？ (And you?) / 他在睡觉呢 (He's sleeping [right now])
嘛 (ma) — "obviously" / "as you know": 这是常识嘛 (That's just common sense, isn't it)

topics.title: Common chengyu
topics.description: Four-character idioms (成语) for everyday Chinese

guide.intro: Chengyu (成语, chéng yǔ) are four-character set phrases — the bite-sized literary references that pepper everyday Chinese. They're not optional flavor: native speakers reach for them in casual chat, news headlines, business emails, and parental scoldings alike. Learn 20-30 high-frequency ones at B2 and you'll start hearing them everywhere.

sections.text: What makes a chengyu different from a regular phrase?

Three things. First, the form is fixed: you can't swap words or change the order. Second, the meaning is rarely the sum of the characters — you have to know the story or convention. Third, they pack a lot into four syllables, which is why they're popular in writing.
Treat chengyu like English idioms: "spill the beans" doesn't literally mean spilling beans. The same logic applies to 画蛇添足 ("draw a snake, add feet").
Where chengyu slot into a sentence
Most chengyu act as a predicate or adverbial — they describe an action or situation. They often sit after the subject, sometimes after 是 / 就是 to label something.

rows.source: 他这样做简直是画蛇添足。
rows.pinyin: Tā zhèyàng zuò jiǎnzhí shì huà shé tiān zú.
rows.translation: What he did was simply gilding the lily.

rows.pinyin: Xué yǔyán bù néng bàn tú ér fèi.
rows.translation: You can't give up halfway when learning a language.

rows.source: 在国外旅行要入乡随俗。
rows.pinyin: Zài guówài lǚxíng yào rù xiāng suí sú.
rows.translation: When traveling abroad, do as the locals do.

sections.text: Strategy for learning them

items: Learn the story — it'll make the meaning stick.
Memorize one example sentence per chengyu — the slot matters more than the dictionary gloss.
Don't overuse them. One chengyu per paragraph is plenty; stacking three sounds try-hard.
Listen for them in TV shows and news headlines — they're frequent in both.

sections.text: Don't translate English idioms into chengyu word-for-word. "Kill two birds with one stone" maps to 一举两得, not 杀两鸟一石.

topics.title: B2 review
topics.description: Stitch the patterns together: 越…越, 不仅…而且, 即使…也, 尽管, formal register

lessons.title: Pattern roundup
lessons.description: Pick the right connector

exercises.prompt: the pattern to its meaning
Pick the right connector for a real fact: "___ 下雨，他还是去跑步了"
exercises.explanation: It's a real fact (it actually rained), so 尽管 / 虽然. 即使 would be hypothetical.

exercises.prompt: Pick the right connector: "___ 下雨，我也要去" (you don't yet know if it'll rain)
Pick the right connector: "他 ___ 努力工作，___ 收入很高"
exercises.explanation: Adding two positive qualities → 不仅...而且. The other connectors don't fit "works hard AND earns well" as a parallel additive pair.

exercises.prompt: Build the connector sentence "He not only is smart, he also is hardworking" (use 不仅...而且)
exercises.answer: 他 不仅 聪明 而且 努力
exercises.explanation: 不仅 must pair with an additive (而且 / 还 / 也). It cannot pair with the contrastive 但是 — they push in opposite directions.

exercises.prompt: the connector to its required partner
"环保 ___ 来 ___ 重要" (越…越 pattern)
exercises.explanation: 环保越来越重要 — "environmental protection is more and more important". Both halves of the 越 frame are required.

exercises.prompt: Which is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: 越来越 already intensifies. Adding 很 doubles up. Drop one or the other.

exercises.prompt: Build "On one hand, the salary is high; on the other hand, the pressure is also great"
exercises.answer: 一方面 工资 很 高 另一方面 压力 也 很 大

exercises.prompt: "___ 人工智能 发展 得 很 快, ___ 不 能 完全 取代 人类"
exercises.explanation: Real fact (AI develops fast) + contrast (can't replace humans) → 尽管/虽然...但是 frame.

exercises.prompt: Pick the layered scenario translation: "Even if you disagree, in my view this is still the right thing to do":
options: 即使你不同意，在我看来这也是正确的事
exercises.answer: 即使你不同意，在我看来这也是正确的事
exercises.explanation: Multi-clause B2: 即使...也 (even if...still) + 在我看来 (in my view) — combining concession with opinion-stating in one breath.

exercises.prompt: Tap the connector pair you hear
exercises.spokenText: 不 仅 而 且
options: 不 仅 而 且
尽 管 但 是
虽 然 但 是
exercises.answer: 不 仅 而 且
exercises.explanation: 不仅...而且 — the additive pair. Identifying which connector pair you hear is the first step to parsing complex sentences quickly.

exercises.prompt: Quick review — pick the version that handles ASPECT + RESULT correctly: "I finished the book"
exercises.explanation: 看完 (read-finish) marks the result; 了 marks completion. "我看了那本书" only means "I read the book" — completion is ambiguous.

exercises.prompt: Final trap: "This morning I had a video call with him for an hour." Pick the natural ordering:
options: 今天早上我跟他视频了一个小时。
我视频他今天早上一个小时。
我跟他一个小时今天早上视频。
一个小时我跟他今天早上视频了。
exercises.answer: 今天早上我跟他视频了一个小时。
exercises.explanation: Time (今天早上) comes first, subject (我) next, coverb phrase (跟他), then verb + duration. English-style trailing time/duration doesn't transfer.

exercises.source: 即使你不同意，在我看来这也是正确的事
exercises.answer: Even if you disagree, in my view this is still the right thing to do
acceptableAnswers: Even if you don't agree, I think this is the right thing
Even with your disagreement, I still see this as right

exercises.prompt: Build "He's not only smart, he's also hardworking"
exercises.answer: 他 不仅 聪明 而且 努力

exercises.prompt: Which is GRAMMATICALLY WRONG?
exercises.explanation: 越来越 already intensifies — adding 很 doubles up.

exercises.prompt: Connector quiz: "___ 下雨, 我 也 要 去" (hypothetical)
exercises.explanation: Hypothetical → 即使. Real fact → 尽管 / 虽然.

exercises.answer: Environmental protection is getting more and more important
acceptableAnswers: Environmentalism is more important than ever

levels.name: C1 — Advanced
levels.description: Operate in Mandarin for business, academic, and journalistic contexts. Argue a position, structure formal discourse, and use 成语 with confidence.

topics.title: Business Chinese
topics.description: Meetings, negotiation, and formal correspondence

guide.intro: Business Mandarin lives in a register far above everyday speech. The same idea you'd say with 因为...所以 over coffee gets dressed up with 鉴于... 因此 in a meeting. Three habits define the register: connectives that tie clauses together, nominalized topics with 至于, and a default to 您 / 贵 honorifics.

sections.text: Formal causal connectives

Casual Chinese uses 因为 X 所以 Y. In formal writing and meetings, you upgrade to 鉴于 X，因此 Y ("in view of X, therefore Y") or 由于 X，故 Y ("owing to X, hence Y"). 因此 and 故 are interchangeable for "therefore", but 故 sounds bookish.

rows.source: 鉴于市场环境的变化，我们因此调整了战略。
rows.pinyin: Jiànyú shìchǎng huánjìng de biànhuà, wǒmen yīncǐ tiáozhěng le zhànlüè.
rows.translation: In view of market changes, we have therefore adjusted our strategy.

rows.source: 由于成本上升，公司因此决定提价。
rows.pinyin: Yóuyú chéngběn shàngshēng, gōngsī yīncǐ juédìng tíjià.
rows.translation: Owing to rising costs, the company has accordingly decided to raise prices.

rows.source: 因为成本上升，所以我们涨价了。
rows.pinyin: Yīnwèi chéngběn shàngshēng, suǒyǐ wǒmen zhǎngjià le.
rows.translation: Because costs rose, we raised prices. (casual)

sections.text: 然而 vs 但是 — "however"
但是 works in any register. 然而 is the formal cousin you reach for in reports, op-eds, and presentations. 不过 sits in between — written Chinese friendly but not stiff.

rows: Strong contrast in essays, news, reports.

sections.text: 至于 — topic shift

至于 X ("as for X") moves the spotlight to a new sub-topic and is heavily used in structured talks. The phrase always introduces a fresh clause and is followed by a comma. Think of it as the spoken equivalent of a slide transition.

rows.source: 营收方面我们超出预期。至于成本，仍需进一步控制。
rows.pinyin: Yíngshōu fāngmiàn wǒmen chāochū yùqī. Zhìyú chéngběn, réng xū jìnyībù kòngzhì.
rows.translation: On revenue we exceeded expectations. As for costs, they still need to be controlled further.

rows.source: 至于您提到的合作方式，我们下周再深入讨论。
rows.pinyin: Zhìyú nín tídào de hézuò fāngshì, wǒmen xiàzhōu zài shēnrù tǎolùn.
rows.translation: As for the form of cooperation you mentioned, let us discuss it in depth next week.

sections.text: 贵 — honorific prefix

贵 ("honored") attaches to nouns referring to the other party's affiliations: 贵公司 (your company), 贵校 (your school), 贵姓 (your honored surname). Use 贵 anywhere a respectful tone is owed; in return, refer to your own side with the humble 敝 (敝公司 "my humble company") or simply 我方 ("our side").
Mixing registers will make you sound off. Once you open a meeting with 贵公司, stay in formal mode: keep using 您, swap 但是 for 然而, and lean on 至于 for transitions.
